exposure: mode of delivery (normal vaginal delivery vs. Cesarean section)
cohort: The study participants were preschool children, categorized based on their birth history as either full-term normal delivery or full-term Cesarean section.
finding: Children born by Cesarean section showed a statistically significant higher tactile sensitivity compared to children born by normal vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: The study concluded that tactile sensitivity is more common in infants delivered by Cesarean section than in infants born by normal vaginal delivery.
